November 2018 (Writing Case note)

Allen Mathis

61 yo retired cabinet maker.

Personal History:

Married, lives with family

Ex-smoker (smoked for 35 yrs, quitted 7yrs ago)

Mother and grandmother had DM.

Medical history:

Poorly controlled DM

Mild-Moderate HTN

Ischemic Heart disease

2011: had coronary artery angioplasty after acute MI

2012: cataract surgery

Fungal infection on foot. Went po—— therapy

FBG - > 5-25mmol

HbA1c -10%



Presenting complaints:

Worsening of Dysponea, decreased exercise tolarence, ankle edema for 2 months.

Can’t sleep lie down (orthopnoea) for past few days.

No chest pain .



Medications:

Inj. Novorapid

Inj. Lantus

Metformin

Metoprolol

Aspirin

Rosuvastatin

Nifedipine

Hydrochlorothiazide
 
3.11.18

Objectives:

Temp : 36.8

BMI : obese>30

BP 148/98

Chest : apex beat shifted laterally with ejection systolic murmur. Bibasal crepitations .

Bilateral Ankle edema

ECG: T inversion in antero-lateral leads. No Q wave, no ST elevation ( changed from 6 months ago)

Assessment : Biventricular heart failure with possible silent ischemia with sustained HTN and poorly
controlled DM



Plan: refer to emergency cardiologist for urgent assessment and advice on management of acute
heart failure and possible silent myocardial Ischemia.



Referral letter to

Cardiologist,

Emergency department

Central hospital

Stillwater.

For urgent assessment and advice on Mx.
